description.p: It’s hard to remember, but there are more of us than I sometimes think. Every time, I get surprised when there are more of us than just me and the people I confide in.
Note: The following are pieces of writing that I’ve put together over the past month and change from a variety of uses, and have been edited to fit into a blog post.

Ok, this is a pretty big title. To be honest, I’m less interested in contributing to the larger-scale discourse on active learning vs direct instruction. I’m more interested in trying to make my teaching a bit more cohesive, fitting into the themes I’m trying to build throughout a short semester with students. Two important ones that I think about a lot are:

It’s the end of the ‘25-‘26 Academic Year, and I’m trying to take a bit of time to reflect on the semester and the year as a whole. Most of the time, my reflections are only meant for myself, scribbled down in my notebook for me to look back on as I prep for future semester. This year, though, I’m trying to share some portions of those.

We’re coming up to the end of the Spring semester and the end of the 2025-2026 academic year (technically the Summer 2026 semester is included, but I’m not teaching this summer, so this is the end of the teaching year for me). I normally try to take some time to reflect on the year. It’s a good time for me to revisit the way I try to build a classroom culture, or what I can do to focus on students’ humanity, or some aspect of my syllabus that is still bugging me.

item.title: My Meeting with a Publisher Rep

description.p: This post is based on something I wrote on social media that I wanted to expand on a bit. You can read the thread on Bluesky here, but I have some more thoughts.
I was reminded of the Four Color Theorem the other day. I wasn’t thinking about maps. I wasn’t thinking about about graphs of any kind, honestly.

My college hosts a professional development day every semester for faculty and staff, and this semester’s is…interesting. There’s a theme for the day, normally something connected loosely with a recent college goal or broad focus. This semester, it’s “Approaching AI with Teamwork and Heart.”

I love teaching Calculus II. It hits the perfect sweet-spot of “has really cool mathematics” and “always available to teach,” since we run multiple sections of it every semester and, apparently, nobody else in my department really likes teaching it that much. Weird. Anyways, it’s my favorite class to teach.
